description:
compiler2 can compare two BackendPrograms only by raw struct equality, which
means raw `Ty` ids. That is sound for ONE narrow case -- two compiles of the
same input, same binary, one process, where the only thing that can renumber
the arena is nondeterminism (see
`compiling_the_same_root_twice_publishes_byte_identical_backend_programs`). It
is the wrong comparand for anything durable.

A `Ty` is an arena index in one `World`. Across two worlds it carries no
meaning: one extra incidental intern anywhere shifts every later id without
changing what the program means. So today there is NO way to ask "are these two
builds equivalent?" across processes, versions, or a cache.

## Why `{:?}` cannot be the canonical form

Measured while closing fz-f98.19: take the Debug rendering and substitute every
`Ty(n)` with `types.display(Ty(n))`. The two renderings still differ, at
1,703,778 characters each, and the first difference is

    value_demands: {ValueId(70): ...   vs   value_demands: {ValueId(11): ...

`HashMap`'s Debug order is per-instance `RandomState` order, so the RENDERING is
unstable even when the structs are equal (they are: struct equality passes). A
canonical form has to be built, not derived from Debug.

## What is wanted

An ordered, structural serialization of `BackendProgram` in which no interned id
appears -- types by their canonical `Types::display` rendering, maps emitted in
a deterministic key order, everything else by structure. Then:

- artifact EQUIVALENCE (do two builds mean the same thing?) is that form's
  bytes, and it survives renumbering, cross-process and cross-version;
- artifact IDENTITY (is this the same build?) is a hash of it, which is what a
  compile cache or a distributed build would key on;
- a failure diff becomes legible. Closing fz-f98.19 required writing a
  throwaway Python multiset differ because a 1.5MB struct inequality names
  nothing.

Note the two properties are genuinely different and BOTH are worth having.
fz-f98.19's defect -- the same 836 types minted in a permuted order -- would be
INVISIBLE under canonicalization, because every position renders the same. That
is the point: canonical form measures the artifact, raw ids measure the
bookkeeping, and determinism of the work order (the job-order test) measures the
cause. Adding this must not delete either existing test.

## Not the answer

A global after-the-fact renumbering pass over the interner arena. It is a
barrier that needs the whole arena, it invalidates `Ty` as a stable handle for
every memo keyed by it, and it would leave the work order nondeterministic while
making only the ids look stable.

## Checks

- A canonical rendering exists for `BackendProgram` with no interned id in it,
  and is stable across two in-process compiles by construction (no sort of
  Debug text).
- A test proves two compiles produce the identical canonical form.
- The existing raw-equality and job-order tests still pass and are documented as
  measuring different properties.
- `dump.rs`'s existing render_* helpers are reused or folded in rather than
  duplicated -- check before writing a second renderer.
title: No canonical externalized form for BackendProgram: equivalence can only be asked as raw Ty struct equality
